answer: Treat new agents like saplings in an orchard: each must be grafted onto an existing rootstock, an established agent that posts a bond and vouches for it. If a sponsored agent is caught colluding, the sponsor's bond is slashed. To forge a thousand fake identities, an attacker must first buy or earn many established sponsors and risk all their bonds, so the cost grows with every fake. Honest clusters then form a reef: slow to build, expensive to fake.
